minor.issue: Decorator stacking bug: @_register('admin_outbound', ...) and @_register('security_runbook_monitor_report', ...) are BOTH applied to build_security_runbook_monitor_report_email. Result: TEMPLATE_CATALOG['admin_outbound']['builder'] now resolves to build_security_runbook_monitor_report_email instead of build_admin_outbound_email. Verified at runtime: TEMPLATE_CATALOG['admin_outbound'] label='Admin Outbound Reply' but builder points at the security function. LATENT — no live regression today because routes/email_tab.py imports build_admin_outbound_email directly and passes template_key='admin_outbound' as a metadata string only. However, any future consumer that calls send_catalog_template(recipient, 'admin_outbound', body=..., original_subject=...) would silently send a Security Runbook Monitor report instead of a support reply. Fix: move the @_register('admin_outbound', ...) decorator onto build_admin_outbound_email (line 7869) — the decorator is currently orphaned above the wrong function.

rca of the issue: USER-REPORTED BUG: Users received confusing 'Support Reply' emails containing raw '## ' markdown headings and '**RED**' bold syntax with 'Global Security Incident Plan — Go-Live Runbook (Amber → Green)' content, every 3 hours. RCA: routes/security_key_rotation.py's run_security_runbook_monitor_cycle (scheduler cadence 3h) was borrowing build_admin_outbound_email (a support-reply template with a hard-coded 'The RealAICoach team has responded to your inquiry...' framing) and stuffing the raw runbook markdown into its body, so users saw a support-conversation subject + framing containing raw markdown. FIX (verified): (a) new dedicated build_security_runbook_monitor_report_email builder with v7 wrap, RAG-colored alert panel, structured snapshot/metrics/risks/milestones/compliance tables, and 'not a support conversation' labeling; (b) send path switched to new builder with template_key='security_runbook_monitor_report' and dedupe_key='runbook-monitor-{run_id}'; (c) noise control gates scheduler-triggered runs to email only on rag_change OR first daily_summary of the UTC day; manual runs always email; suppressed runs are recorded with suppressed=true, send_reason=None, success=false. Verified in DB: last three scheduler runs today all correctly suppressed (RAG unchanged RED, one email already sent today at 06:19Z manual).
